reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the core premises: it demonstrates that stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) in a W-based refractory HEA achieve 2.15 GPa strength and 15% ductility, and explains the mechanism via coherent interfaces facilitating dislocation transmission and multistage strain hardening. However, the evidence does not address impact-induced energy release, so that premise is unsupported.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates can be induced in W-based refractory HEAs by stepwise thermo-mechanical processing
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations
Coherent nanoprecipitates generate progressive multistage strain hardening that delays strain localization
This approach improves ductility without sacrificing high strength in W-based refractory HEAs
The treated alloy retains impact-induced energy release characteristics
